q: A Money Bill can be introduced only in:

options.C: Either House of Parliament
options.D: A joint sitting of both Houses

e: A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and only with the recommendation of the President.

q: The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha, with its recommendations, if any, within a period of:

options.C: 14 days

e: The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha with its recommendations, if any, within fourteen days of receiving it.

q: The power of the Union Government to raise loans on the security of the Consolidated Fund of India is derived from Article ______ of the Constitution:
e: Article 292 of the Constitution gives the Union Government the power to borrow on the security of the Consolidated Fund of India within limits fixed by Parliament.

q: Under Article 284 of the Constitution, moneys received by Government officers in their official capacity, otherwise than as revenues or public moneys (for example, court deposits), are required to be paid into the:

options.C: Departmental account with the accredited bank

e: Under Article 284, moneys received by Government officers in their official capacity, such as court deposits, are paid into the Public Account of India, as the Government holds them in trust.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Moneys standing in the Public Account of India belong to the Government and form part of its own revenue.
2. Disbursements out of the Public Account of India can be made only under appropriation made by Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Both statements are false: Public Account moneys are held in trust and do not belong to the Government, and disbursements from it do not require appropriation by Parliament. Hence neither.

q: Which of the following does NOT form a part of the Consolidated Fund of India?

options.A: Tax revenues received by the Union Government
options.B: Loans raised by the Government of India
options.C: Provident Fund deposits of Government servants
options.D: Non-tax revenues of the Union Government

e: Provident Fund deposits of Government servants are held in the Public Account of India, not the Consolidated Fund, which comprises revenues, loans raised and moneys received in repayment of loans.

q: 'Debt charges' of the Government of India, comprising interest payments on its internal and external debt, are:

options.A: Submitted to the vote of the Lok Sabha like other Demands for Grants
options.B: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Met out of the Public Account of India
options.D: Borne by the Reserve Bank of India

e: Debt charges, being interest payments on the internal and external debt of the Government, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and are not voted.

q: Along with the Annual Budget, the statements presented to Parliament in pursuance of the FRBM Act include the:

options.C: Audit Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General
options.D: Medium-term Fiscal Policy Statement and the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement

e: Under the FRBM Act, the Medium-term Fiscal Policy Statement and the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement are presented to Parliament along with the Annual Budget.

q: The 'Fiscal Deficit' of the Government represents:

options.A: The total borrowing requirement of the Government, being the excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings
options.B: The excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts
options.C: Fiscal deficit minus interest payments
options.D: The excess of capital expenditure over capital receipts

e: Fiscal Deficit is the excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings, and thus represents the total borrowing requirement of the Government for the year.

q: Which of the following is a 'non-debt capital receipt' of the Government?

options.C: Disinvestment proceeds
options.D: Ways and Means Advances from the Reserve Bank

e: Disinvestment proceeds are non-debt capital receipts because they reduce Government assets without creating any liability, unlike market borrowings or Treasury Bills.

q: In the accounts of the Union Budget, the earnings of the Indian Railways are classified as:

options.C: Capital receipts

e: Railway earnings are a receipt of the Government from its commercial operations and are classified as non-tax revenue under revenue receipts in the Union Budget.

q: The Final Modification Estimates, carried out in January, are based broadly on the actuals of the first ______ months of the financial year:

options.C: Eight

e: The Final Modification Estimates in January are based broadly on the actuals of the first nine months of the financial year, April to December.

q: A 'New Instrument of Service' means:

options.A: A substantial expansion or extension of an existing service or activity, as distinct from an entirely new service
options.B: An entirely new activity which was not contemplated in the budget
options.C: A new Plan Head opened in the classification of accounts
options.D: A new fund created by the Government

e: A New Instrument of Service means a substantial expansion or extension of an existing service or activity, as distinct from an entirely new service, and requires prior approval at the prescribed level.

q: Re-appropriation of funds is permissible only:

options.A: Between two different Demands for Grants
options.B: From 'charged' expenditure to 'voted' expenditure and vice versa
options.C: Within the same grant (Demand) voted by Parliament
options.D: From capital expenditure to revenue expenditure in all cases

e: Re-appropriation is allowed only within the same grant voted by Parliament; it cannot be made between different Demands or between charged and voted expenditure.

q: The original grant under a Demand is Rs 1,200 crore. During the year, a supplementary grant of Rs 80 crore is obtained and funds of Rs 45 crore are surrendered. The Final Grant for the Demand is:

options.C: Rs 1,280 crore

e: Final Grant = Original Grant + Supplementary Grant - Surrender = Rs 1,200 crore + Rs 80 crore - Rs 45 crore = Rs 1,235 crore.

q: Through-traffic earnings of Rs 9,000 are to be apportioned among Railways X, Y and Z in proportion to the distances travelled over them — 500 km, 300 km and 200 km respectively. The share of Railway Z is:
e: Total distance = 500 + 300 + 200 = 1,000 km. Share of Z = Rs 9,000 x 200 / 1,000 = Rs 1,800.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Vote of Credit is granted where, on account of the magnitude or the indefinite character of a service, the demand cannot be stated with the details ordinarily given in a Demand for Grant.
2. An Exceptional Grant, like an ordinary grant, forms part of the services of the current financial year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Statement 1 is true: a Vote of Credit is granted where the demand cannot be stated with ordinary detail. Statement 2 is false: an Exceptional Grant is for a special purpose and does not form part of the services of the current year. Hence 1 only.

q: In the railway accounting system, 'internal check' over expenditure is exercised by the Accounts Department:

options.A: Only after the close of the financial year
options.C: At the pre-payment stage, before bills are passed for payment
options.D: Only in respect of works expenditure

e: Internal check in railways is exercised by the Accounts Department at the pre-payment stage, when bills are checked before being passed for payment.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Balances under suspense heads are reviewed periodically (half-yearly) with a view to securing their clearance.
2. The balances outstanding under the debt, suspense and remittance heads are reported through the Debt Head Report.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Both statements are true: suspense balances are reviewed half-yearly for clearance, and balances under debt, suspense and remittance heads are reported through the Debt Head Report.

q: Works financed from the Development Fund of the Railways are generally:

options.A: Works expected to earn a high financial return
options.B: Works financed only through market borrowings
options.C: Works charged to Major Head 5002 in all cases
options.D: Necessary works which may not be directly remunerative, such as passenger amenities and staff welfare works

e: The Development Fund finances necessary works which may not be directly remunerative, such as passenger amenities, labour welfare and operational improvement works.

q: The accounts of the Indian Railways are maintained on the:

options.C: Purely memorandum cash system
options.D: Accrual system prescribed for companies under the Companies Act

e: Railway accounts are maintained on the double-entry (commercial) system of accounting, unlike the largely cash-based accounts of the general Government.

q: Differences noticed between the balance under 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' as per the railway books and the statement of the Reserve Bank's Central Accounts Section are adjusted through the head:

options.C: Traffic Suspense

e: Differences between the balance under Deposits with Reserve Bank in the railway books and the Reserve Bank Central Accounts Section statement are adjusted through Reserve Bank Suspense.

q: 'Internal check' differs from 'internal audit' mainly in that internal check:

options.A: Is carried out by the staff of the Comptroller and Auditor General
options.B: Is an integral part of the accounting system itself, exercised at the time the transaction is entered into and paid, whereas internal audit is a subsequent review
options.C: Is exercised only once in five years

e: Internal check is an integral part of the accounting system itself, operating when the transaction is entered into and paid, whereas internal audit is a subsequent review of completed transactions.

q: The Cash & Pay Office of a zonal railway functions as a part of the:

options.C: Engineering Department

e: The Cash & Pay Office of a zonal railway, which handles cash receipts and payments, functions as a part of the Accounts Department.

q: Loans raised by the Government of India, forming its public debt, are credited to the:

options.C: Consolidated Fund of India

e: Loans raised by the Government of India form its public debt and are credited to the Consolidated Fund of India.

q: In the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, Capital Outlay on Indian Railways — Strategic Lines is classified under Major Head:
e: Capital Outlay on Indian Railways - Strategic Lines is classified under Major Head 5003, while Major Head 5002 covers capital outlay on commercial lines.

q: For linking the capital accounts of the Railways with the accounts of the Central Government, the Plan Heads of the railway classification function, under Major Heads 5002 and 5003, as the:

options.C: Primary Units

e: For linking railway capital accounts with the Central Government accounts, the Plan Heads function as the Minor Heads under Major Heads 5002 and 5003.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Works expenditure is classified under Major Heads 5002/5003 and the respective Plan Heads irrespective of whether it is financed from Capital, the Depreciation Reserve Fund, the Development Fund, the Railway Safety Fund or the RRSK.
2. A work financed from the Development Fund is classified under Major Head 3002, as the Development Fund is fed by appropriations from revenue.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Statement 1 is true: works expenditure is classified under Major Heads 5002/5003 with the relevant Plan Head whatever the source of finance. Statement 2 is false: a Development Fund work is not classified under Major Head 3002. Hence 1 only.

q: In the Government accounts, the portion of capital outlay on the Railways which is met from the Railway Funds (Depreciation Reserve Fund, Development Fund, Capital Fund and the like) is adjusted under Major Head 5002 through minor heads styled as:

options.B: 'Deduct — Amount met from' the respective Fund
options.C: 'Suspense — Railway Funds'

e: The portion of capital outlay met from Railway Funds is adjusted under Major Head 5002 through minor heads styled 'Deduct - Amount met from' the respective Fund, so the gross outlay remains visible.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Reservation fees and superfast supplementary charges collected from passengers form part of the Passenger (Coaching) Earnings of the Railways.
2. Tatkal charges collected from passengers are classified under Sundry Other Earnings of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Statement 1 is true: reservation fees and superfast supplementary charges form part of Passenger (Coaching) Earnings. Statement 2 is false: Tatkal charges also form part of Passenger Earnings, not Sundry Other Earnings. Hence 1 only.

q: Sundry Other Earnings of a zonal railway are:

options.A: Apportioned among all the zonal railways in proportion to distance
options.B: Credited wholly to the Railway Board
options.C: Credited wholly to the railway on which they accrue, as they are not subject to apportionment
options.D: Credited to the Development Fund of the Railways

e: Sundry Other Earnings are credited wholly to the railway on which they accrue, as they are local in nature and are not subject to apportionment among railways.

q: Under the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh (RRSK), of the assured annual outlay of Rs 20,000 crore, the contribution from Gross Budgetary Support is:

options.C: Rs 10,000 crore

e:
Of the assured RRSK outlay of Rs 20,000 crore a year, Rs 15,000 crore comes from Gross Budgetary Support and the balance from the Railways' internal resources.
Update: the figures in this question describe the original RRSK design (assured outlay Rs 20,000 crore a year: Rs 15,000 crore GBS + Rs 5,000 crore internal resources). RRSK's currency has since been extended for a further five years w.e.f. 2022-23, with total Gross Budgetary Support of Rs 45,000 crore. (Source: Ministry of Railways, Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question No. 138, answered 02.02.2024.)

q: The contribution of about Rs 5,000 crore of the Railways towards the corpus of the Special Railway Safety Fund (SRSF) was raised mainly through:

options.A: Market borrowings raised by the Indian Railway Finance Corporation
options.C: Appropriations from the Railway Pension Fund
options.D: A safety surcharge levied on passenger fares

e: The Railways' contribution of about Rs 5,000 crore to the Special Railway Safety Fund corpus was raised mainly through a safety surcharge levied on passenger fares.

q: On the closure of the Special Railway Safety Fund in the year 2008, its unspent balance was transferred to:

options.A: The Capital Fund of the Railways
options.C: The general revenues of the Government of India
options.D: The Depreciation Reserve Fund of the Railways

e: On closure of the Special Railway Safety Fund in 2008, its unspent balance was transferred to the Depreciation Reserve Fund of the Railways.

q: The balances accumulated in the National Small Savings Fund are invested in:

options.B: Equity shares of public sector undertakings
options.C: Loans and advances to railway public sector undertakings

e: Balances accumulated in the National Small Savings Fund are invested in Central and State Government securities, so small savings collections finance Government borrowing.

q: The National Small Savings Fund was established in the Public Account of India with effect from:

options.C: 1 April 2004

e: The National Small Savings Fund was established in the Public Account of India with effect from 1 April 1999 to account for small savings collections separately.

q: Part B of the Finance Minister's Budget Speech deals with:

options.A: The general state of the economy
options.B: The statements laid under the FRBM Act
options.C: The Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways
options.D: The taxation proposals for the ensuing year

e: Part B of the Finance Minister's Budget Speech contains the taxation proposals for the ensuing year, while Part A gives an overview of the economy and policy announcements.

q: The Budget document which explains the various other Budget documents and the terms used in them is known as:

options.C: Key to Budget Documents

e: The Key to Budget Documents explains the various Budget documents and the technical terms used in them, helping the reader understand the Budget papers.

q: The Budget Division, which is responsible for the preparation of the Union Budget, functions in the:

options.C: Department of Revenue

e: The Budget Division, responsible for preparation of the Union Budget, functions in the Department of Economic Affairs of the Ministry of Finance.

q: The Economic Survey of India is prepared by the Economics Division of the Department of Economic Affairs under the guidance of:

options.C: The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India

e: The Economic Survey is prepared by the Economics Division of the Department of Economic Affairs under the guidance of the Chief Economic Adviser.

q: Under Article 112 of the Constitution, the Annual Financial Statement is caused to be laid before both Houses of Parliament by:

options.B: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.C: The Prime Minister

e: Under Article 112, the Annual Financial Statement is caused to be laid before both Houses of Parliament by the President, and the Finance Minister presents it on his behalf.

q: A Bill which, if enacted and brought into operation, would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India cannot be introduced or moved except on the recommendation of:

options.C: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

e: A Bill involving expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India cannot be introduced or moved in Parliament except on the recommendation of the President.

q: Which of the following subjects cannot be dealt with in a Money Bill under Article 110 of the Constitution?

options.A: The imposition, abolition or alteration of any tax
options.B: The appropriation of moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: The creation of an All-India Service
options.D: Declaring any expenditure to be expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India

e: Article 110 defines a Money Bill by subjects like taxation, borrowing and appropriation; creation of an All-India Service is not among them and is dealt with under a separate constitutional provision.

q: The Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement, laid before Parliament under the FRBM Act, sets out:

options.A: Three-year rolling targets for specified fiscal indicators
options.B: The monthly expenditure plans of the Ministries
options.C: The Demands for Grants of all Ministries
options.D: The outcome targets of Centrally Sponsored Schemes

e: The Medium-term Fiscal Policy Statement, laid under the FRBM Act, sets out three-year rolling targets for specified fiscal indicators such as fiscal deficit and revenue deficit.

q: Ways and Means Advances made by the Reserve Bank of India under Section 17(5) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 are repayable:

options.A: Within thirty days of the advance
options.B: Within one year of the advance
options.C: Not later than three months from the date of making the advance
options.D: At any time on demand by the Reserve Bank

e: Ways and Means Advances under Section 17(5) of the RBI Act must be repaid not later than three months from the date of the advance.

q: The system of Ways and Means Advances for the Central Government, introduced with effect from 1 April 1997, replaced the earlier system of:

options.C: Dated Government securities

e: The Ways and Means Advances system introduced from 1 April 1997 replaced the earlier system of ad hoc Treasury Bills, which had automatic monetisation of the deficit.

q: The first Railway Convention Committee after Independence was constituted in the year:
e: The first Railway Convention Committee after Independence was constituted in 1949 to review the financial relationship between the Railways and General Finances.

q: The Railway Convention Committee is an ad hoc Parliamentary committee which is constituted:

options.A: By the President under Article 263 of the Constitution
options.B: By the Railway Board through an office order
options.C: By the Finance Commission along with its report
options.D: On a resolution adopted by the Lok Sabha and concurred in by the Rajya Sabha

e: The Railway Convention Committee is constituted on a resolution adopted by the Lok Sabha and concurred in by the Rajya Sabha.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A debit balance under the suspense head 'Reserve Bank Suspense' represents amounts debited by the Reserve Bank, that is, payments made by it on behalf of the Railways, which are pending adjustment in the railway books.
2. A credit balance under the head 'Reserve Bank Suspense' represents amounts credited by the Reserve Bank to the Railways' account which are pending adjustment in the railway books.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Both statements are true: a debit balance under Reserve Bank Suspense represents payments made by the Reserve Bank on behalf of the Railways pending adjustment, and a credit balance represents amounts credited by the Bank pending adjustment.

q: An error of classification in the books of a railway, that is, the booking of an item of expenditure under a wrong head of account:

options.A: Prevents the Trial Balance of the railway from agreeing
options.B: Does not affect the agreement of the Trial Balance, since the total debits and total credits remain equal
options.C: Is brought to light automatically by the Trial Balance
options.D: Can be rectified only with the sanction of the Railway Board

e: An error of classification does not affect the agreement of the Trial Balance, because the entry is still posted with equal debits and credits, only under a wrong head.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Every entry in the Journal Book of a railway must be supported by a Journal Voucher duly signed by an Accounts Officer.
2. Journal Vouchers and cash vouchers are numbered in one common serial series.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Statement 1 is true: every Journal entry must be supported by a Journal Voucher duly signed by an Accounts Officer. Statement 2 is false: Journal Vouchers and cash vouchers are numbered in separate serial series. Hence 1 only.

q: The daily statement of receipts and payments rendered by the accredited bank to the Accounts Office, from which the bank's transactions are reconciled with the railway books, is known as the:

options.C: Debt Head Report

e: The daily statement of receipts and payments sent by the accredited bank to the Accounts Office is the Bank Scroll, used for reconciling bank transactions with the railway books.

q: The Registers of Earnings, Revenue Allocation Registers, Registers of Works and Suspense Registers maintained in the Accounts Office of a railway are classified as:

options.C: Initial records of the executive departments

e: Registers of Earnings, Revenue Allocation Registers, Registers of Works and Suspense Registers are subsidiary records supporting the General Books and the Ledger.

q: The primary responsibility for showing the correct allocation, that is, the head of account, on a bill or voucher rests with:

options.A: The Accounts Officer who passes the bill for payment
options.B: The executive (departmental) officer who presents the bill
options.C: The Cash & Pay Office which makes the payment

e: The primary responsibility for showing the correct head of account on a bill rests with the executive officer who presents the bill; the Accounts Office checks it during internal check.

q: The original grant under a Demand is Rs 950 crore. During the year, a supplementary grant of Rs 55 crore is obtained and funds of Rs 20 crore are surrendered. The Final Grant for the Demand is:

options.C: Rs 1,005 crore

e: Final Grant = Original Grant + Supplementary Grant - Surrender = Rs 950 crore + Rs 55 crore - Rs 20 crore = Rs 985 crore.

q: Through-traffic earnings of Rs 12,000 are to be apportioned among Railways X, Y and Z in proportion to the distances travelled over them, namely 700 km, 300 km and 200 km respectively. The share of Railway Y is:
e: Total distance = 700 + 300 + 200 = 1,200 km. Share of Y = Rs 12,000 x 300 / 1,200 = Rs 3,000.

q: The surrender of anticipated savings out of a sanctioned grant:

options.A: Is an executive act and does not require the approval of Parliament
options.B: Requires the vote of the Lok Sabha
options.C: Requires a Supplementary Demand for Grants
options.D: Can be made only after the Appropriation Accounts of the year are finalised

e: Surrender of anticipated savings out of a sanctioned grant is an executive act of the competent authority and does not require the approval of Parliament.

q: A Money Bill can be introduced in the Lok Sabha only:

options.A: By any member of the House
options.B: By the Chairman of the Estimates Committee
options.C: By a Minister, that is, it can only be a Government Bill
options.D: By a member authorised by the President

e: A Money Bill can be introduced in the Lok Sabha only by a Minister, that is, it can only be a Government Bill, and with the President's recommendation.

q: The Contingency Fund of India, established under Article 267 of the Constitution, is regulated by:

options.B: The Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950
options.C: The FRBM Act, 2003
options.D: The Appropriation Act of the year concerned

e: The Contingency Fund of India, placed at the disposal of the President under Article 267, is regulated by the Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950.

q: Dividends received by the Government of India from railway public sector undertakings, such as IRCTC and IRFC, are classified in the Union Government accounts as:

options.B: Sundry Other Earnings of the Railways
options.C: Non-tax revenue receipts
options.D: Receipts under the Public Account of India

e: Dividends received from railway PSUs such as IRCTC and IRFC are income of the Government and are classified as non-tax revenue receipts.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sub-Major Head 01 under Major Head 5002 represents capital bearing dividend liability.
2. Sub-Major Head 02 under Major Head 5002 represents capital free of dividend liability.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Both statements are true: under Major Head 5002, Sub-Major Head 01 represents capital bearing dividend liability and Sub-Major Head 02 represents capital free of dividend liability.

q: The amount granted by Parliament through a Vote on Account:

options.A: Is in addition to the total grant voted for the year
options.B: Is expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Lapses if it is not spent within one month of the grant
options.D: Forms part of the total grant for the year and is merged in it when the full grant is voted

e: A Vote on Account is not in addition to the annual grant; it forms part of the total grant for the year and is merged in it when the full grant is voted.

q: The Estimates Committee of Parliament consists of:

options.A: 15 members, all from the Rajya Sabha
options.B: 22 members drawn from both Houses of Parliament
options.C: 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha
options.D: 45 members drawn from both Houses of Parliament

e: The Estimates Committee consists of thirty members, all elected from the Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha has no representation on it.

q: Treasury Bills of the Government of India are issued in maturities of:

options.C: One year, three years and five years

e: Treasury Bills of the Government of India are issued in three maturities: 91 days, 182 days and 364 days.

q: Cash Management Bills, issued by the Government of India to meet temporary mismatches in its cash flow, have a maturity period of:

options.C: Less than 91 days

e: Cash Management Bills are issued to meet temporary cash flow mismatches and have a maturity of less than 91 days.

q: Coaching Earnings of the Railways comprise:

options.A: Passenger Earnings and Other Coaching Earnings
options.C: Goods Earnings and Sundry Other Earnings
options.D: Passenger Earnings and Sundry Other Earnings

e: Coaching Earnings comprise Passenger Earnings and Other Coaching Earnings such as parcels, luggage and other coaching services; Goods Earnings are accounted separately.

q: The earnings collected at a station are required to be:

options.A: Utilised for meeting the contingent expenditure of the station
options.B: Remitted in full to the Cash Office or the accredited bank, and not utilised for local expenditure
options.C: Retained at the station till the close of the financial year
options.D: Adjusted against the imprest held by the Station Master

e: Station earnings must be remitted in full to the Cash Office or the accredited bank and cannot be retained or used for meeting local expenditure of the station.

q: In the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, the Special Railway Safety Fund was maintained in the Public Account of India under Major Head:
e: The Special Railway Safety Fund was maintained in the Public Account of India under Major Head 8230, which covers funds for specific purposes held in the Public Account.

q: Supplementary Demands for Grants, unlike the main Demands for Grants presented with the Budget, are:

options.A: Examined by the Public Accounts Committee before they are voted
options.B: Voted only by the Rajya Sabha
options.C: Presented only during the Budget session of Parliament
options.D: Voted by the Lok Sabha without prior examination by the Departmentally Related Standing Committees

e: Supplementary Demands for Grants are voted by the Lok Sabha without prior examination by the Departmentally Related Standing Committees, unlike the main Demands presented with the Budget.

q: Postings in the Ledger of a railway are made from:

options.A: The Station Balance Sheets rendered by the stations
options.B: The bank scrolls received from the accredited bank
options.C: The Works Registers maintained in the Accounts Office
options.D: The closing totals of the Journal and the Classified Abstract

e: Postings in the Ledger are made from the closing totals of the Journal and the Classified Abstract, which summarise the transactions of the month head-wise.

q: The original grant under a Demand is Rs 1,050 crore. During the year, a supplementary grant of Rs 70 crore is obtained and funds of Rs 35 crore are surrendered. The Final Grant for the Demand is:

options.C: Rs 1,050 crore

e: Final Grant = Original Grant + Supplementary Grant - Surrender = Rs 1,050 crore + Rs 70 crore - Rs 35 crore = Rs 1,085 crore.

q: Through-traffic earnings of Rs 8,000 are to be apportioned among Railways X, Y and Z in proportion to the distances travelled over them — 400 km, 250 km and 150 km respectively. The share of Railway Z is:
e: Total distance = 400 + 250 + 150 = 800 km. Share of Z = Rs 8,000 x 150 / 800 = Rs 1,500.

q: The Final Grant under a Demand for a year is Rs 640 crore and the actual expenditure booked against the Demand is Rs 672 crore. The excess expenditure, which will require regularisation through an Excess Grant, is:

options.C: Rs 36 crore

e: Excess expenditure = Actual expenditure - Final Grant = Rs 672 crore - Rs 640 crore = Rs 32 crore, to be regularised through an Excess Grant.

q: In the accounts of the Government of India, the revenue receipts (earnings) of the Strategic Lines of the Railways are classified under Major Head:
e: Revenue receipts of the Strategic Lines are classified under Major Head 1002, while Major Head 1001 covers the earnings of the commercial lines of the Railways.

q: The administrative expenses of the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, including the salaries and allowances of the Comptroller and Auditor General and the persons serving in that office, are:

options.A: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: Submitted to the vote of Parliament every year
options.C: Met out of the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Shared equally between the Union and the States

e: The administrative expenses of the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General, including salaries of the CAG and his staff, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India to safeguard the independence of the office.

q: The salaries and allowances of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha are:

options.A: Submitted to the vote of the Lok Sabha every year
options.B: Met out of the Public Account of India
options.C: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: Paid out of the Contingency Fund of India

e: Salaries and allowances of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and are not submitted to the vote of the House.

q: The pensions payable to or in respect of the Judges of the Supreme Court of India are:

options.A: Submitted to the vote of Parliament every year
options.B: Charged on the Consolidated Funds of the States
options.C: Met out of the Public Account of India
options.D: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India

e: Pensions of the Judges of the Supreme Court are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, so that they are not dependent on the annual vote of Parliament.

q: Besides the items of expenditure specified in the Constitution itself, expenditure on any other service can be declared to be 'charged' on the Consolidated Fund of India by:

options.B: The Finance Minister by a notification
options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Besides the items charged by the Constitution itself, expenditure on any other service can be declared charged on the Consolidated Fund of India only by Parliament by law.

q: Supplementary Demands for Grants are ordinarily presented to Parliament during the course of a financial year in:

options.C: Three batches

e: Supplementary Demands for Grants are ordinarily presented to Parliament during a financial year in three batches.

q: A Demand for Grant, after it has been passed (voted) by the Lok Sabha, becomes:

options.C: A Vote on Account

e: A Demand for Grant passed (voted) by the Lok Sabha becomes a Grant; the Appropriation Act then authorises withdrawal of the granted and charged amounts from the Consolidated Fund.

q: Part A of the Finance Minister's Budget Speech deals mainly with:

options.A: The taxation proposals for the ensuing year
options.B: The detailed Demands for Grants of the Ministries
options.C: The provisions of the Finance Bill, clause by clause
options.D: An overview of the economy and the major policy announcements of the Government

e: Part A of the Budget Speech gives an overview of the economy and the major policy announcements of the Government; the taxation proposals come in Part B.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 109 of the Constitution lays down a special procedure for the passage of Money Bills in Parliament.
2. The Rajya Sabha may amend a Money Bill, and the Lok Sabha is bound to accept the amendments so made.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Statement 1 is true: Article 109 lays down the special procedure for Money Bills. Statement 2 is false: the Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes, and the Lok Sabha may accept or reject them. Hence 1 only.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Public Accounts Committee consists of twenty-two members, fifteen elected from the Lok Sabha and seven from the Rajya Sabha.
2. By convention, since 1967, the Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee is a member of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Both statements are true: the Public Accounts Committee has twenty-two members, fifteen from the Lok Sabha and seven from the Rajya Sabha, and by convention since 1967 its Chairman is from the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways consists of thirty-one members — twenty-one drawn from the Lok Sabha and ten from the Rajya Sabha.
2. The recommendations contained in the report of the Committee are binding, and a Demand for Grant cannot be voted until the report has been accepted by the Government.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Statement 1 is true: the Standing Committee on Railways has thirty-one members, twenty-one from the Lok Sabha and ten from the Rajya Sabha. Statement 2 is false: its recommendations are advisory, not binding. Hence 1 only.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, the declared provisions of the Finance Bill relating to customs and excise duties take effect from the expiry of the day on which the Bill is introduced in the Lok Sabha.
2. If the Finance Bill is not enacted within seventy-five days of its introduction, the declared provisions cease to have the force of law and the excess collections made under them are refundable.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Both statements are true: under the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, declared customs and excise provisions take effect from the expiry of the day of introduction, and lapse if the Finance Bill is not enacted within seventy-five days, making excess collections refundable.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A cheque issued by the Railways remains valid for payment for three months from the date of its issue.
2. A cheque which remains uncashed beyond its period of validity is treated as time-barred, and its amount is written back in the books through a transfer entry.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Both statements are true: a railway cheque is valid for three months from its date of issue, and an uncashed time-barred cheque is written back in the books through a transfer entry.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Budget document 'Receipts Budget' presents a detailed analysis of the tax revenues, non-tax revenues and capital receipts of the Government.
2. The Budget document 'Key Features of Budget' contains the detailed head-wise estimates of expenditure of every Ministry.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Statement 1 is true: the Receipts Budget analyses tax revenues, non-tax revenues and capital receipts in detail. Statement 2 is false: Key Features of Budget is only a summary document, not detailed head-wise estimates. Hence 1 only.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'Vote on Account' from a 'Vote of Credit'?

options.A: A Vote on Account is a grant in advance, for a part of the financial year, pending completion of the budgetary process; a Vote of Credit is a blanket (lump-sum) grant for meeting an unexpected demand, the particulars of which cannot be stated in the ordinary way
options.B: A Vote on Account is granted only in an election year; a Vote of Credit is granted in every year
options.C: A Vote on Account covers both receipts and expenditure; a Vote of Credit covers expenditure only
options.D: A Vote on Account is voted by both Houses of Parliament; a Vote of Credit is voted by the Rajya Sabha alone

e: A Vote on Account is a grant in advance for a part of the year pending completion of the budgetary process, whereas a Vote of Credit is a blanket lump-sum grant for an unexpected demand whose particulars cannot be stated in the ordinary way.

q: In railway accounts, 'earnings' differ from 'receipts' in that:

options.A: Earnings are accounted only in the books of the Railway Board, whereas receipts are accounted at the stations
options.B: Earnings relate to goods traffic only, whereas receipts relate to all traffic
options.C: Earnings are always smaller than receipts
options.D: Earnings represent the amounts earned for the services rendered, as brought to account from the station and traffic returns, whereas receipts represent the cash actually realised and remitted

e: Earnings represent the amounts earned for services rendered, as brought to account from station and traffic returns, whereas receipts represent the cash actually realised and remitted.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'Classified Abstract' from the 'Trial Balance' in railway accounts?

options.A: The Classified Abstract is prepared at the close of the year only, whereas the Trial Balance is prepared every month
options.B: The Classified Abstract is a head-wise summary of the transactions of the month, compiled from the subsidiary books, from which the General Books are posted; the Trial Balance is a statement of the balances of the Ledger accounts, prepared to prove the arithmetical accuracy of the books
options.C: The Classified Abstract is maintained by the executive departments, whereas the Trial Balance is maintained by the Audit
options.D: The Classified Abstract records only cash transactions, whereas the Trial Balance records only transfer transactions

e: The Classified Abstract is a head-wise summary of the month's transactions compiled from the subsidiary books, from which the General Books are posted; the Trial Balance lists the balances of Ledger accounts to prove the arithmetical accuracy of the books.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the monthly 'Account Current' of a zonal railway from the 'Debt Head Report'?

options.A: The Account Current is the complete monthly account of the receipts and disbursements of the railway rendered to the Railway Board, whereas the Debt Head Report shows only the balances outstanding under the debt, deposit, suspense and remittance heads
options.B: The Account Current is rendered once a year, whereas the Debt Head Report is rendered every month
options.C: The Account Current is prepared by the Audit, whereas the Debt Head Report is prepared by the executive departments
options.D: The Account Current shows only the suspense balances of the railway, whereas the Debt Head Report shows its earnings

e: The Account Current is the complete monthly account of receipts and disbursements rendered by a zonal railway to the Railway Board, whereas the Debt Head Report shows only the balances outstanding under the debt, deposit, suspense and remittance heads.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'suspense heads' from 'remittance heads' in railway accounts?

options.A: Suspense heads are operated only by the Railway Board, whereas remittance heads are operated only by the divisions
options.B: Suspense heads record cash in transit, whereas remittance heads record amounts awaiting classification
options.C: Suspense heads record transactions which are held temporarily pending their clearance to the final heads of account, whereas remittance heads record transactions in the course of settlement between accounting units, such as moneys remitted from one unit to another
options.D: There is no difference between the two; both record transactions in the course of settlement

e: Suspense heads record transactions held temporarily pending clearance to their final heads of account, whereas remittance heads record transactions in the course of settlement between accounting units, such as moneys remitted from one unit to another.

q: The estimates of expenditure in the Detailed Demands for Grants are exhibited:

options.A: Net of all recoveries, the recoveries not being shown at all
options.B: Only for the charged portion of the expenditure
options.C: Only in terms of the net cash outgo from the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: On a gross basis, the recoveries being shown separately as 'Deduct' entries to arrive at the net amount of the Demand

e: Estimates in the Detailed Demands for Grants are exhibited on a gross basis, and recoveries are shown separately as 'Deduct' entries below the gross amount to arrive at the net Demand.

q: The Detailed Demands for Grants exhibit, for each head of account, the figures relating to:

options.A: The Budget Estimates for the ensuing year only
options.B: The Actuals of the preceding year, the Budget Estimates and the Revised Estimates of the current year, and the Budget Estimates of the ensuing year
options.C: The Actuals of the last five years
options.D: The Final Grant and the actual expenditure of the preceding year

e: For each head, the Detailed Demands for Grants show the Actuals of the preceding year, the Budget Estimates and Revised Estimates of the current year, and the Budget Estimates of the ensuing year.

q: The Budget document 'Expenditure Profile' mainly presents:

options.A: A snapshot (broad overview) of the pattern of the total expenditure of the Government, ministry-wise and scheme-wise
options.B: The detailed estimates of the Ministry of Railways alone
options.C: The provisions of the Finance Bill explained clause by clause
options.D: The recommendations of the Finance Commission

e: The Expenditure Profile presents a broad snapshot of the pattern of the Government's total expenditure, ministry-wise and scheme-wise, rather than detailed head-wise estimates.

q: A Vote on Account granted by the Lok Sabha:

options.A: Authorises the Government to levy taxes for a part of the financial year
options.B: Covers the estimates of receipts as well as of expenditure
options.C: Authorises withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India for meeting expenditure for a part of the financial year, pending completion of the budgetary process; it does not deal with the taxation proposals
options.D: Is required only when a new Government is formed after a general election

e: A Vote on Account authorises withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India for expenditure for a part of the financial year pending completion of the budgetary process, and does not deal with taxation proposals.

q: A Vote on Account is ordinarily:

options.A: Voted after a detailed discussion of each Demand for Grant
options.B: Examined by the Public Accounts Committee before being voted
options.C: Voted by the Rajya Sabha alone
options.D: Passed by the Lok Sabha without the detailed discussion which the Demands for Grants undergo

e: A Vote on Account is passed by the Lok Sabha without the detailed discussion which the individual Demands for Grants undergo before voting.

q: The Finance Bill, though introduced in the Lok Sabha immediately after the presentation of the Budget, is taken up for consideration and passing:

options.A: Before the general discussion on the Budget takes place
options.B: After the Appropriation Bill has been passed
options.C: Only after the close of the financial year
options.D: Along with the Vote on Account, before the Demands are discussed

e: The Finance Bill is taken up for consideration and passing only after the Appropriation Bill has been passed, so that the tax proposals are voted after the grants are authorised.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. No discussion on the Budget takes place in Parliament on the day on which it is presented.
2. During the general discussion on the Budget which follows, no motion can be moved and no voting on the Demands for Grants takes place.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2

e: Both statements are true: no discussion takes place on the Budget on the day it is presented, and during the general discussion that follows, no motion can be moved and no voting on Demands takes place.

q: The members of the Estimates Committee of Parliament are:

options.A: Elected every year by the Lok Sabha from amongst its own members
options.B: Nominated by the President for a term of five years
options.C: Elected by both Houses of Parliament sitting together
options.D: Appointed by the Speaker from amongst the members of the Rajya Sabha

e: The members of the Estimates Committee are elected every year by the Lok Sabha from amongst its own members, in accordance with the principle of proportional representation.
